newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Indonesia mulls partial autonomy for Timor - paper.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia mulls partial autonomy for Timor - paper.

text.p: Indonesia is considering a proposal to grant partial autonomy to its troubled territory of East Timor, Jakarta's special ambassador for Timor Francisco Lopes de Cruz said in an interview published on Saturday.

Lopes de Cruz told the Portuguese weekly Expresso that President Suharto had agreed to review East Timor's status for the first time with a view to granting it an autonomy similar to that of the island of Java.
"The government has already agreed to consider Timor a region with special autonomy within the scope of Indonesian law," he told the newspaper.
The remarks follow the award last week of the Nobel Peace Prize to two East Timor independence campaigners, a decision which angered Jakarta.
Lopes de Cruz stressed that even if Suharto ratified the proposed changes, Timor would remain part of Indonesia which annexed the former Portuguese colony in 1976.

"A local parliament would only be able to approve measures governing development, foreign investment and education," he said. Matters of foreign policy, justice, defence and finance would remain in Jakarta's hands.
Timorese resistance leader Jose Ramos-Horta, who won the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize together with Bishop Carlos Belo, immediately poured cold water on the proposal.
"Autonomy can only be a subject for discussion when Timor's position as Indonesia's 27th province ceases to be a condition," Ramos-Horta told Expresso.
East Timor has bedevilled Indonesia's international relations since it invaded the territory in December 1975 and formally annexed it in July 1976.
The United Nations does not recognise Indonesian rule in East Timor, which lies about 500 kms (300 miles) north of Australia, and regards Portugal as the administering power.
